label: rem:ring-closure-superstability
title: Topological reorganisation, super-stability, and the spring analogy
html:
Remark. Topological reorganisation, super-stability, and the spring analogy

The spring analogy. The open chain is a spring held apart. Closing it into a ring snaps the spring shut. The separate coils merge into a single tighter winding.

Ring super-stability from threading. For N = 6, crossing weight drops from 5 to \approx 3, providing additional stabilisation. Breaking the ring requires dissolving the threading link entirely back into N separate Hopf links. The threading link is a lower-energy encoding of the binding. Reverting to the pairwise encoding costs energy.

The barrier: topological reorganisation. The transition \mathcal{C}_N \to \mathcal{R}_N requires a discontinuous change in topology. The braid word changes from a product of non-adjacent generators to the correlated product (\sigma_1 \cdots \sigma_{N-1})^2.
